newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sage up in heavy trade lifted by bookovers. [CORRECTED 13:43 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sage up in heavy trade lifted by bookovers. [CORRECTED 13:43 GMT]

text.p: South African financial services company Sage Group Ltd was firm on Thursday with heavy volumes traded in a number of bookovers done by broker SMK Securities Ltd.
(Corrects name of broker in first and third paragraph from "Senekel Mouton" to "SMK Securities Ltd".)
Dealers said the volumes could be related to a possible buyout by Samgro Investment Holdings Ltd.

"It could be related to (Samgro chairman) Christo Wiese who is trying to buy Sage. The deals were done by SMK Securities Ltd who is his broker. But the shares are only about two percent of the company," one dealer said.
Sage shares were last up 25 cents to 26.25 rand with 3.4 million shares valued at 85 million rand changing hands.
Wiese, through Samgro Investment Holdings, created the country's fifth largest bank through the merger of NBS Holdings Ltd and Boland Bank this year.
NBS Boland is 15 percent owned by Samgro which has rights to raise its stake to 34.9 percent.
